evidence.title: ‘Lawyers should be running to courts’ to stop coal approvals after landmark ruling, NSW MP says

occurrences.checkable_against: High Court of Australia case records and judgments involving climate change
occurrences.quote_span: A landmark decision in Australia’s first climate change high court case has been described as a clear message to governments and fossil fuel companies that exported greenhouse gas emissions “cannot simply be ignored”.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Australia High Court Mount Pleasant coalmine expansion ruling

occurrences.checkable_against: NSW Court of Appeal proceedings and High Court case records concerning the Mount Pleasant coalmine expansion
occurrences.quote_span: The coal company brought the high court case after a local community group, the Denman Aberdeen Muswellbrook Scone Healthy Environment Group (Dams Heg), halted the coalmine expansion on climate grounds in the NSW court of appeal.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Australia High Court Mount Pleasant coalmine expansion ruling

occurrences.checkable_against: Murray Watt’s statement and Australian government ministerial records
occurrences.quote_span: Murray Watt, the federal environment minister, said on Wednesday afternoon that while he had not had an opportunity to review the judgment in full, “the decision from the high court is in relation to a New South Wales government decision based on New South Wales legislation”.
occurrences.speaker: Murray Watt
occurrences.subject: Australia High Court Mount Pleasant coalmine expansion ruling

occurrences.checkable_against: High Court of Australia judgment on MACH Energy’s Mount Pleasant coalmine expansion approval
occurrences.quote_span: On Wednesday morning, the nation’s highest court ruled that the approval of MACH Energy’s Mount Pleasant coalmine expansion in NSW’s Hunter Valley was invalid, in a judgment that sets a precedent for fossil fuel projects in the state.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Australia High Court Mount Pleasant coalmine expansion ruling

occurrences.checkable_against: Chris Bowen’s public statement on the High Court judgment
occurrences.quote_span: “The law of the land is law of the land, as interpreted by the high court, and we respect that.
occurrences.speaker: Chris Bowen
occurrences.subject: Australia High Court Mount Pleasant coalmine expansion ruling

occurrences.checkable_against: Steph Hodgins-May’s public statement about the High Court judgment
occurrences.quote_span: “This judgment sends a clear message to governments and fossil fuel companies that the climate impacts of their projects cannot simply be ignored or pushed down the line.”
occurrences.speaker: Steph Hodgins-May
occurrences.subject: Australia High Court Mount Pleasant coalmine expansion ruling

occurrences.checkable_against: High Court of Australia judgment on MACH Energy’s Mount Pleasant coalmine expansion approval
occurrences.quote_span: In a 3-2 split ruling, the high court found the state’s Independent Planning Commission (IPC) failed to consider imposing conditions to minimise greenhouse gas emissions that would be generated by the mine when the coal is sold and burnt overseas.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Australia High Court Mount Pleasant coalmine expansion ruling

occurrences.checkable_against: Australian national greenhouse gas inventory methodology
occurrences.quote_span: Known as scope 3 emissions, these are not counted in Australia’s domestic tally.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Australia High Court Mount Pleasant coalmine expansion ruling

occurrences.checkable_against: NSW Environmental Planning and Assessment Act and legislative amendment records
occurrences.quote_span: arguing that the Minns government should amend NSW’s Environmental Planning and Assessment Act to “make clear that overseas emissions from Australia’s exported resources are not a consideration in project approvals”.
occurrences.speaker: Angus Taylor and Matt Canavan
occurrences.subject: Australia High Court Mount Pleasant coalmine expansion ruling

occurrences.checkable_against: Australian government records and Fiji climate negotiations attendance records
occurrences.quote_span: The climate change minister, Chris Bowen, who is in Fiji chairing climate negotiations, said: “The law of the land is law of the land, as interpreted by the high court, and we respect that.
occurrences.speaker: Chris Bowen
occurrences.subject: Australia High Court Mount Pleasant coalmine expansion ruling

occurrences.checkable_against: Murray Watt’s statement and applicable Commonwealth and NSW legislation
occurrences.quote_span: “It doesn’t automatically transfer to commonwealth decisions or commonwealth legislation,” he told News24.
occurrences.speaker: Murray Watt
occurrences.subject: Australia High Court Mount Pleasant coalmine expansion ruling

occurrences.checkable_against: Joint statement by Angus Taylor and Matt Canavan and subsequent government legislative action
occurrences.quote_span: In a joint statement, the Liberal leader, Angus Taylor, and the Nationals leader, Matt Canavan, described the decision as a threat to “Australia’s standing as a reliable energy exporter” and said the federal and NSW governments “must act immediately to fix the law”.
occurrences.speaker: Angus Taylor and Matt Canavan
occurrences.subject: Australia High Court Mount Pleasant coalmine expansion ruling
